konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: 9M-2026 revenue was Rp5,102.0bn, +9.7% yoy [F28, F70, S4], but the LK does not publish quarterly physical volumes and the growth is not volume-led: KPC revenue rose to Rp3,588.0bn from Rp3,088.0bn while KPC's own FY2025 mine output fell (overburden 102.16 from 106.33 million bcm, coal 10.51 from 11.21 Mt), and Arutmin revenue was Rp1,395.0bn against Rp1,357.9bn on flat tonnage [F31, F32, F71, F72, F74, F75, F84, F85, S3, S4]. Third-party revenue fell to Rp119.0bn from Rp204.4bn [F33, F86, S4]. The 9M growth is therefore rate, mix and the Arutmin extension, not a volume cycle. FY2026E +8.5% carries the 9M run-rate into a seasonally stronger Q4 but below the nine-month pace; FY2027E +5% is a real-rate step-up on flat-to-down client volumes, and FY2028E-FY2030E decelerate to +4%, +3.5% and +3% as the 2026 coal RKAB of about 600 Mt from about 790 Mt [F38, F39, S3] and the 1 January 2027 state-exporter transition through PT DSI [S7] cap client offtake. No FY2027E-FY2030E mine-plan volume schedule is public; we do not invent one and instead hold volumes flat with rate inflation. LT 3.0% is IDR CPI plus modest real growth, below the macro deck's nominal GDP anchor.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The in-sourcing turnaround is the single biggest margin driver: FY2025 gross margin was 15.05% on revenue of Rp6,392.8bn and COGS of Rp5,430.6bn [F1, F3, S5], while 9M-2026 gross margin reached 20.28% (revenue Rp5,102.0bn, COGS Rp4,067.2bn) [F28, F58, S4] as subcontractor cost fell to Rp593.4bn from Rp1,137.8bn in the nine-month 2025 comparative and the owned fleet took over more waste removal [F62, S4, S6]. The input is stated AT FY2025 BASE FUEL COSTS, as the template requires. An input of 22.6% reproduces the realised 9M-2026 effective margin of 20.28% once the deck's FY2026 Brent (96.0) is put through the 15%/50% oil link; the previous 22.2% input was about half a point too low. We then hold the input flat in nominal terms for FY2027E-FY2030E and the long run: costs stay at the last actual in real terms, as the method card requires. The effective margin therefore moves only with the oil link (higher in FY2027E at the lower Brent deck), not through a default wage or biodiesel squeeze. There is no sourced cost line that justifies a multi-point decline.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Fuel is a direct COGS line of Rp210.75bn in 9M-2026 (5.2% of Rp4,067.2bn COGS) [S4] and diesel also sits inside equipment rental (Rp378.0bn) and hauling (Rp427.1bn) [S4]. Adding the contractor-supplied fuel embedded in those two lines gives about 15% of COGS exposed to Brent; the rest (depreciation, wages, repairs, subcontractors) is not oil-linked.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Operating agreements with KPC and Arutmin are rate-based and renewed periodically; the company absorbed the 2025 B40 cost increase without a full rate reset [S3], so only half of the oil exposure is assumed to pass through into service rates in the same year, the balance sits in the margin until the next contract reset.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A was 3.69% of revenue (Rp235.8bn of Rp6,392.8bn) [S5]; 9M-2026 was 6.32% (Rp322.4bn of Rp5,102.0bn) [S4], including a jump in salaries and wages (Rp208.8bn vs Rp116.5bn) and a new depreciation charge in G&A after the fleet purchase. Note 27 of the interim LK explains neither the salary step nor any one-off item, so we do not assume it reverses: the input is held at the observed nine-month run-rate. That removes the earlier unsourced normalisation, which was the largest value-positive departure in the base.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: D&A is the data pack's biggest error: Yahoo carries Rp19.1bn for FY2025 because the LK uses the direct cash-flow method. The LK prints the components separately, fixed-asset depreciation of Rp861.96bn (S5 p.89) plus right-of-use depreciation of Rp78.71bn (S5 p.92), and F9 carries their combined FY2025 total of Rp940.67bn, which is the figure the model uses; F9 is therefore cited for the combined total, not for the fixed-asset component alone, and adding F10 on top of it would double-count. The company's own EBITDA bridge of Rp1,752.6bn less operating profit of Rp726.4bn [F88, F89, S3] implies about Rp1,026bn of total non-cash charge, i.e. a further ~Rp85bn of amortisation/other non-cash that the LK does not print as a single line. 9M-2026 printed totals were Rp826.2bn of fixed-asset depreciation plus Rp19.1bn of right-of-use depreciation, 16.6% of 9M revenue [F110, F111, S4]. FY2026E 15.5% of revenue (higher Q4 revenue dilutes the ratio), easing to 15.0% LT as the fleet depreciates on a straight-line basis; the model's FY2025 da line uses the F9 combined total, with the residual to the company bridge disclosed in §3 rather than forced into D&A.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex peaked with the two fleet batches: Rp1,588.9bn in FY2025 (24.9% of revenue) and Rp1,436.0bn in FY2024 [F11, F12, S5], and 9M-2026 was Rp1,341.6bn [F52, S4], flat with the 9M-2025 Rp1,338.2bn and equal to 26.3% of 9M revenue, not a step-down. The Oct-2026 Rp149.2bn Bank Mega investment credit to subsidiary PT DH Kontraktama, explicitly for heavy-equipment purchase, confirms the programme continued after the balance-sheet date [F105, S10]. FY2026E is therefore set at 25% of revenue, close to the 9M run-rate; FY2027E 21%, then 19%, 18%, 17% and 16% LT as the two batches are complete (fully operational by end-September 2025 [S6]) and spend settles toward a maintenance level for the completed fleet. The October credit is a further heavy-equipment purchase, so the fleet is still growing at the margin, not only being replaced [F105, S10]. LT 16% is above D&A at 15% of revenue [F9], so the fleet is maintained rather than run down.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The 9M-2026 balance sheet shows operating working capital of Rp21.8bn, effectively zero against Rp5,102.0bn of revenue [S4]; FY2025 was negative (Rp-227.6bn) because related-party receivables and payables net close. A contractor paid by two related-party mine operators has no structural working-capital build, so 0% is the anchor.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Indonesia's corporate rate is 22%; 9M-2026 tax expense of Rp146.8bn on PBT of Rp659.9bn is a 22.2% effective rate [S4]. FY2025's apparent tax benefit is the deferred-tax effect of the negative goodwill, not a sustainable rate [S5].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The 9M-2026 finance cost of Rp319.4bn [F61, S4] is a nine-month charge, not an annual rate: annualised on opening debt of Rp3,559.4bn it is about 12.0%, and on average debt of about Rp4,095bn about 10.4%. The new Bank Mega equipment credit signed on 29 October 2026 carries 10% per annum [F106, S10], and the July-2025 syndicated facility was 8.3% but was repaid on 22 January 2026 [S3]. 10.0% is the blended marginal rate used for the P&L interest charge in the forecast only; it does not replace the cost of debt in the WACC, which continues to use the house 9.45% pre-tax rate (val.coc.kd_pre_tax), so the house floor still sets the discount rate.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 9M-2026 finance income of Rp5.57bn on opening cash of Rp1,590.6bn is a 0.35% nine-month yield [S4]; the operating cash balance is largely transactional, so 1.0% is already generous against the realised run-rate and well below the BI rate of 5.75% in the macro deck.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: In the first nine months of 2026 the company drew Rp5,041.7bn of long-term bank loans and repaid Rp3,984.6bn, a net debt increase of Rp1,071bn, while cash fell by Rp845.7bn from Rp1,590.6bn to Rp744.9bn [F34, S4 p.13]. The net increase in net debt over the nine months is therefore Rp1,917bn, not Rp1,000bn. FY2026E carries Rp1,917bn; Q4 is assumed to add no further net borrowing, since the 30 October Rp149.2bn equipment facility is small and drawn by a subsidiary at year-end [F105, S10]. After FY2026E the model assumes no new net borrowing as capex normalises and free cash flow covers debt service. The DCF bridge uses the actual 30 September 2026 net debt of Rp3,885.3bn from gross bank loans of Rp4,574.9bn less cash [F34, F103, F104, S4].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 negative goodwill of Rp4,535.4bn is a non-cash one-off [F18, S5] and is excluded from the forecast; 9M-2026 other income of Rp260.2bn includes a Rp152.9bn unrealised fair-value gain on an investment, also non-recurring [S4]. Forecast set to zero.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests are Rp15.2bn of a Rp8,591.1bn equity base [S5]; the minority share of profit was Rp26.5m in FY2025 [S8 of S3], immaterial at 0.0001.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: There is no fixed dividend policy; the AGM decides [S3]. The FY2025 profit paid a cash dividend of Rp58.57bn [F15, S4]; on reported profit that is trivial, but on underlying recurring profit (before the non-cash negative goodwill) it is roughly a mid-teens payout. The company also returned Rp950.0bn through the 2026 buyback [F93, S3] and spent Rp791.4bn of cash on treasury shares in 9M-2026 alone [F107, S4]. A 16% cash payout is the reconciled base, consistent with the FY2025 capital-return pattern, with the rest funding capex and the GMR programme.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: The 2026 buyback retired 1,638,793,874 shares (4.03% of the issued capital) for Rp950bn, completed 13 February 2026 [S3]; the 30 September 2026 balance sheet carries 39,048.6m shares [S0] against 40,687.4m at end-2025 [F16, S5]. FY2026E -4.03%, then flat.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The house default is 4.0% for an IDR corporate; Indonesia's nominal GDP anchor in the macro deck is about 8.5% (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% CPI), so 4.0% is already a discount to nominal GDP rather than a premium. The previous 3.0% was an unsourced 1pp haircut below the default and below long-run CPI plus real growth; we use the default. The terminal value starts after FY2031, the last year covered by either client licence [F91, F92, S5], and therefore carries renewal risk rather than contracted volume.

challenges.challenge: The revenue path (+10.5% FY2026E, +8% FY2027E, +6.0%, +3.5%, +3.0%) is never decomposed into volume and rate, and the LK's own project data show volumes falling: total overburden 193.85 (2023) to 134.36 (2024) to 138.63 Mbcm (2025), KPC 122.09 to 106.33 to 102.16 Mbcm, and total coal 18.27 to 17.29 to 17.04 Mt [S3 p.10]. The national RKAB was meanwhile cut from 790 to 600 Mt [F38/F39] and coal exports move to PT DSI on 1 Jan 2027 [S7]. The 9M-2026 +9.7% revenue growth may be rate rather than volume, but the report never says which, and §1 cites only the 2025 volume without the trend. Required: split 9M-2026 revenue growth into million bcm / tonnes and Rp per unit, source KPC and Arutmin mine-plan volumes for FY2027E-FY2030E, and show the volumes implied by the growth path; restate the base and bear if volumes are flat to down.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Revenue growth is now decomposed by client and shown to be rate-led: KPC revenue rose to Rp3,588.0bn from Rp3,088.0bn while KPC overburden fell to 102.16 from 106.33 Mbcm and Arutmin revenue rose to Rp1,395.0bn from Rp1,357.9bn on flat tonnage; no quarterly physical volumes are disclosed. Base growth cut to 8.5% FY2026E then 5%, 4%, 3.5% and 3%; FY2027E-FY2030E hold volumes flat with rate inflation and no invented mine-plan schedule; the horizon now ends FY2031 on the dated IUPKs. Report sections 1 and 3 and the assumptions updated.

challenges.challenge: The drift.capex_pct BLOCK is not discharged with a source that says what the justification claims. F52 shows 9M-2026 capex of Rp1,341.6bn against Rp1,338.2bn in 9M-2025 — flat, and at 26.3% of 9M revenue, not stepping down — so the model's FY2026E 20% (Rp1,412.8bn) leaves only Rp71bn for Q4 versus Rp250.7bn in Q4-2025. A subsidiary drew Rp149.2bn of Bank Mega credit to buy heavy equipment on 30 October 2026 (fund record, 2026-10-30/31), which contradicts 'what remains is sustaining/replacement capex' and is missing from post_bs_review. LT capex of 13% is below D&A of 14.5%, i.e. a shrinking fleet while revenue grows 3%. Required: hold FY2026E capex at the 9M run-rate (at least 22-25%) or source the step-down; set LT capex at or above D&A, or source the sub-replacement assumption; add the October equipment loan to post_bs_review.
challenges.answer: Accepted. FY2026E capex raised to 25% of revenue, in line with the 9M run-rate of 26.3%; LT capex set to 16%, above D&A at 15%, so the fleet is maintained rather than run down. The 29-Oct-2026 Rp149.2bn Bank Mega equipment credit (63 months, 10%) is now in post_bs_review and section 3, and the capex justification cites F52 and the loan. The drift.capex_pct BLOCK is justified in qc_justifications.

challenges.challenge: The model's net-debt line contradicts the balance sheet the DCF itself uses. model.lines.net_debt for FY2026E is Rp1,985.7bn, but the DCF bridge uses the 30 September 2026 net debt of Rp3,885.3bn; the net_borrowing input of Rp1,000bn contradicts its own basis text (debt +Rp1,071bn and cash -Rp846bn in 9M-2026 = +Rp1,917bn), and the cash roll-forward omits the Rp950bn buyback. Consequently §3's 'forecast net debt to EBITDA of 0.92x' is wrong: Rp3,885.3bn / FY2026E EBITDA of Rp2,155.2bn = 1.80x, and 9M-2026 interest cover is 2.2x (EBIT Rp712.4bn / finance cost Rp319.4bn), not 'improving'. Required: restate the FY2026E net debt and leverage to the actual, reconcile net_borrowing to Rp1,917bn, include the buyback in the cash roll, and correct the 'leveraged but serviceable' language.
challenges.answer: Accepted. net_borrowing reconciled to Rp1,917bn, equal to the 9M debt increase plus cash decline; the DCF bridge uses actual 30-Sep-2026 net debt of Rp3,885.3bn (bank loans Rp4,574.9bn plus leases less cash of Rp744.9bn); section 3 now states that the model roll is too low because it starts at YE2025 and omits the Rp791.4bn buyback cash, shows the actual leverage and says interest cover is only a little over two times. 'Leveraged but serviceable' removed.

challenges.challenge: The DCF horizon and terminal treatment contradict the only dated contract fact. The Arutmin IUP expires 1 November 2030 and its operating agreement runs only to that date [S3 p.131], yet the DCF runs explicit flows to FY2035 plus a perpetuity: PV of FY2031-35 flows (Rp2,570.1bn) plus terminal value (Rp3,938.9bn) is Rp6,509.0bn, or 68% of the Rp9,541.6bn EV [fund record methods.dcf_fcff]. KPC's operating-agreement term is not disclosed. The §4 statement that terminal value is '41% of EV — a moderate dependence' understates the post-contract-life exposure, and §2's 'we treat that contract base as the asset life' is contradicted by the perpetuity. Required: state the KPC agreement's term and expiry, then either truncate the DCF at the Arutmin licence or source a renewal assumption, disclosing the 68% post-2030 value share and its sensitivity (Arutmin was 27% of 9M-2026 revenue).
challenges.answer: Accepted. Both licence dates sourced: Arutmin IUPK expires 1 November 2030 and KPC IUPK 31 December 2031 (S5 p.378); horizon cut to six explicit years FY2026E-FY2031E; terminal value disclosed at 69.4% of EV and described as renewal, not contracted volume; section 4 states that a reader who does not believe in renewal should strip it out. The section 2 moat text is aligned.

challenges.challenge: §4 misreads the engine's own reverse DCF. The reverse DCF solves on the same dcf_fcff value that includes the full Rp5,380bn GMR bridge, so it does not mark GMR 'near zero'. At the price and with GMR at Rp5,380bn the implied FY2027E growth is 3.66% — above the 2.5% long-run CPI, so the contractor does not 'shrink in real terms' — and the residual contract-business value is about Rp82/share, roughly 3.3x FY2026E EBITDA. Alternatively, holding the contract business at its DCF value (Rp146/share) implies GMR at about Rp74/share, 54% of the bridge, not zero. The bearish framing removes the bull case the reader most needs. Required: show the price decomposition explicitly (GMR and contract business) and correct the 'GMR marked near zero' and 'shrinks in real terms' claims.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The reverse DCF now states implied FY2027E growth of 2.9% (base FY2027E growth of 5.0% less 2.1pp), below CPI of 3.28% and nominal GDP, with GMR held at the full audited bridge. Section 4 decomposes the price: market capitalisation of Rp8.59trn against the GMR bridge of Rp5,380.0bn, which is 62.6% of the market capitalisation, so GMR is not marked near zero and the contract business is what the market discounts. The 'GMR marked near zero' and 'shrinks in real terms' claims are withdrawn.

challenges.challenge: The GMR bridge is carried at probability 1.0 and no scenario or sensitivity tests it. GMR is 'not yet operating' with no resource, reserve or feasibility statement [S5 p.39], was acquired for Rp844.5bn consideration, and is credited at Rp5,380bn — 48.5% of DCF equity value. The bear TP of 324 still carries the full bridge; a write-down is called 'on top' but never quantified. Halving the bridge lowers the weighted 12-month value by about Rp48, the target to about Rp250 and total return to about 14% (BUY to ADD); carrying GMR at its Rp844.5bn consideration gives about Rp224 and about 3% (HOLD). The rating's 30.7% return is only 5.7pp above the 25% BUY threshold. Required: add a quantified GMR-impairment bear (write-down to consideration, or a 50% haircut) and show the target and rating sensitivity; state the ex-GMR value per share in §4.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part and quantified. GMR now has a stated write-back: to the Rp844.5bn consideration removes Rp4,535.4bn of bridge value, about Rp116 per share, which takes the bear value below the current share price; the report calls the rating a GMR-validated BUY with a narrow margin. The engine applies the valuation bridge to every scenario and cannot shock it per scenario, so the impairment is quantified in section 5 rather than in the mechanical bear, and that limitation is disclosed. The bridge probability stays at 1.0 because the method card bars an unsourced haircut on an audited value.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA leg carries 28% weight at a 10.08x peer median the report itself calls inflated. The median is ABMM at 10.08x, not PTRO at 38.7x, so §4's attribution to 'PTRO trades at a konglo premium' is inaccurate, and the set mixes contractors with coal miners (BSSR 6.3x, INDY 9.0x, TEBE 12.9x). Because the leg contributes about Rp125.5 of the Rp318.5 v0, removing it and reweighting DCF/EV-Sales 83/17 lowers v0 to about Rp268 and the target to about Rp241, a total return of about 11% — ADD, not BUY. Required: use a contractor-only peer set, or cut the weight to the level the report's own confidence supports, and restate the target and rating.
challenges.answer: Accepted. EV/EBITDA weight cut from 28% to 15%, EV/Sales to 15% and DCF raised to 70%; the attribution is corrected because the 10.1x median is ABMM, not PTRO; section 4 notes the set mixes contractors and miners and that the EBITDA metric is the engine's FY2025 figure, below the company's own bridge. Target and rating rerun.

challenges.challenge: The konglo ownership map is incomplete and 'no single holder above ten percent' is contradicted by the report's own register. The Feb-2025 PMTHMETD issued 18.83bn shares (46.29%) at Rp75 to MTN (10.09bn, 24.8%), ATP (4.79bn) and AMM (3.96bn) [S3 p.11-12]; the 31 December 2025 register lists no MTN or AMM line, ATP at 8.55%, CIMB Securities at 6.38% and CGS at 5.53% (both appear only after the conversion), and 'public (each below 5%)' at 63.08% [S3 p.77]. Goldwave at 9.38% ('qq. Zurich Assets') plus Zurich at 6.18% is 15.56%, above the 10% the report says is absent. The 'related contractors' label for MTN/ATP/AMM is not supported by S6 p.9, which calls them 'kreditur' (creditors). Required: reconcile where MTN's 24.8% block went, identify the beneficial owners behind CIMB/CGS, aggregate the Zurich-linked holdings, and cite the related-party basis or drop the label; reflect it in the konglo profile.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 6 now reproduces the full 31-December-2025 register (F96-F102), aggregates the Zurich-linked Goldwave and Zurich lines (15.55%) and withdraws 'no holder above ten percent', reconciles the February-2025 placement (MTN 10.09bn shares, 46.29% of post-issue capital, at Rp75) against a register with no MTN or AMM line, states that the block most likely sits in the 63.08% public bucket or was sold and that the transferee is not disclosed, notes that CIMB and CGS beneficial owners are undisclosed, and withdraws the 'related contractors' label because S6 calls the recipients creditors.

challenges.challenge: The buyback is presented as a neutral share-count reduction, but the arithmetic is a large capital-allocation loss: Rp949,999,969,885 for 1,638,793,874 shares is an average of Rp579.7 [S3 p.131], versus Rp220 today (-62%), and the Rp950bn is 11% of the current market cap. The Rp951.7bn treasury stock is pledged to lenders [F67, S4]; at Rp220 the buyback shares are worth about Rp360bn against that carrying value. The report states neither the average price nor any pledge/LTV risk. Required: state the Rp580 average and its mark-to-market, and assess the treasury-pledge coverage and any LTV or covenant trigger, in §5 and §6.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Sections 5 and 6 now state that the buyback spent Rp950.0bn on 1,638.8m shares at an average far above today's Rp220, call it a capital-allocation loss, and mark the treasury stock of Rp951.7bn against a market value far below carrying. The unsupported pledge claim is withdrawn because no reviewed filing discloses a pledge; if one exists, coverage would be weak. No LTV or covenant trigger is disclosed.

challenges.challenge: The gross-margin input falls from 22.2% (FY2026E, at base fuel) to 19.6% LT — effective 19.81% to 18.15%, 2.1pp below the realised 9M-2026 20.28% — on an unquantified 'B40/B50 biodiesel and wages meet a client base that will press rates' narrative [S3, S4]. The method card bars a default margin squeeze and requires costs at the last actual in real terms; the assumptions call this 'not a default squeeze' without a quantified cost line. Required: hold the 9M-2026 effective margin in real terms, or source the decline with a specific biodiesel/wage amount and show its value impact.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The gross-margin input is held at 22.6% for FY2026E and flat thereafter and in the long run; the effective margin reproduces the 9M-2026 20.28% actual once the Brent deck is put through the 15%/50% oil link. There is no default squeeze; the only margin movement is the oil link. The basis is rewritten.

challenges.challenge: Terminal growth is 3.0% 'rather than the 4% house default' to stay below nominal GDP, but 3% is far below Indonesia's roughly 8.5% nominal GDP (5.29% real plus 3.28% CPI in the macro deck) and below the default, with no source for the 1pp haircut; payout is 8% against about 16% of underlying FY2025 NP (Rp58.57bn on about Rp360bn). Both depart from the LK in the value-negative direction. Required: justify the 1pp g haircut with a source or use the default, and reconcile the payout with the FY2025 actual.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Terminal growth restored to the 4% house default and payout raised to 16%, consistent with the FY2025 dividend of Rp58.6bn on underlying profit. No one-point haircut remains.

challenges.challenge: The restated D&A contradicts its own basis. The assumptions cite fixed-asset depreciation of Rp861.96bn plus ROU depreciation of Rp78.71bn [F9/F10], but model.lines.da for FY2025A is Rp861.96bn, so FY2025 EBITDA is Rp1,584.2bn versus Rp1,662.9bn with ROU — and the company's own EBITDA bridge is Rp1,752.6bn [S3], a Rp168.4bn gap. The calibration gate's actual margin (24.8%) is therefore understated, and the EV/EBITDA metric of Rp1,584.2bn understates that leg by about Rp44/share (about Rp11 on the target). Required: include ROU (and reconcile to the company's bridge) in the restated history, then rerun calibration and the EV/EBITDA cross-check.
challenges.answer: Accepted in full after the Q10/Q15 fact fix. F9 now carries the combined FY2025 D&A of Rp940.67bn (fixed-asset depreciation of Rp861.96bn plus right-of-use depreciation of Rp78.71bn), so model FY2025A D&A is Rp940.67bn and EBITDA is Rp1,667.1bn (EBIT Rp726.4bn plus D&A), within 4.9% of the company's Rp1,752.6bn bridge; the residual unprinted amortisation is disclosed in section 3 rather than forced into D&A. Calibration and the EV/EBITDA cross-check were rerun after the fix.

challenges.challenge: 'Our fundamental twelve-month value is Rp373, so the stock trades at 0.68x value' is wrong: 220 / 373 = 0.59x. The 0.68x is price over value today (Rp321.6 per share, model.valuation.konglo.v_fundamental), not over the twelve-month value; §4 repeats the error ('price at 0.68x the fundamental twelve-month value of Rp373'). Required: use 0.59x against the Rp373 twelve-month value, or 0.68x against the current value, consistently in the summary and §4.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The summary and section 4 now separate the current fundamental value (Rp269.8) from the twelve-month value (Rp311.9): the price is 0.82x the current value, not 0.59x or 0.68x against the twelve-month figure. The wording is consistent in both places.

challenges.challenge: FY2027E growth of +8% is justified in the assumptions as 'the first full year of the two in-house fleet batches', but S6 says all heavy equipment was fully operational by end-September 2025, making FY2026 the first full year. The growth timing is misdated, and the real FY2027E driver — volume, rate or the Arutmin renewal — is not sourced. Required: correct the basis and source the FY2027E volume and rate assumptions.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The FY2027E 'first full year of the fleet' basis is deleted because S6 says the second batch was fully operational by end-September 2025, making FY2026 the first full year. FY2027E growth is now a real-rate step-up on flat-to-down client volumes, sourced to the dated contracts and the RKAB and DSI constraints; no FY2027E-FY2030E mine-plan volumes are public and none are invented.

challenges.challenge: The scenario set violates the mirrored-shock rule on the largest value driver. GMR (48.5% of DCF equity) is not a scenario driver at all: the bear's write-down is described as 'on top' but the bull never gets the mirrored validation, and both TPs carry the full bridge. A GMR resource statement that confirms the appraisal is worth up to about Rp138/share before the lens, and is excluded from the bull TP of 430. Required: add a GMR shock (for example -30% / +30%) to both bear and bull, or state and source why the asymmetry is justified.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part, on the same mechanical constraint as C6. The engine applies the valuation bridge to every scenario and cannot shock it per scenario, so the mirrored GMR shock is not in the table. Section 5 instead quantifies both directions: a write-back to consideration removes Rp4,535.4bn and takes the bear below the current price, while a validating resource statement adds upside of the same order and is excluded from the bull. The limitation is disclosed explicitly. A per-scenario bridge shock would need an engine change; flagged as unresolved.

challenges.challenge: The cost-of-debt basis is a period error: '9M-2026 finance cost of Rp319.4bn against opening debt of Rp3,559.4bn is 9.0%' is a nine-month ratio; annualised on opening debt it is 12.0%, and on average debt (about Rp4,095bn) 10.4%. The engine floors the input to 9.45% for the WACC. Required: annualise the cost of debt or cite the marginal facility rate (the 8.3% syndicated facility) as the sole basis, and reconcile to the 2.2x current interest cover.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The cost of debt is set to 10.0% (the 9M charge annualises to about 10.4% on average debt; the new Bank Mega facility carries 10%); the 9.0% period error is removed. Interest expense rises in the model and sections 3 and 4 reconcile interest cover of a little over two times using 9M gross profit less G&A against the finance cost.

challenges.challenge: The two market-capitalisation sentences publish a broken number: both render "IDR8,590,700,881.40tn" (rendered Investment summary and §4; the QC Q13 defect and judge FIX 1). {{mkt.mcap_idr}} is the full-rupiah value Rp8,590,700,881,400 and |idrtn divides by 1e3 rather than 1e12, so the printed figure is nine orders of magnitude too large and the sentence's own conclusion ("the asset accounts for more than half of the equity value") reads as nonsense against it. The underlying value (Rp8.59trn on 39,048.6m shares at Rp220) and the conclusion are right; the rendering is not. The defect is house-wide (ABMM Q9) but it must not publish here.
challenges.answer: Both market-capitalisation sentences now render {{mkt.mcap_idr|idrb}} and print IDR8,590.7bn in the Investment summary and section 4. A grep of fund record, fund record and fund record finds no remaining |idrtn use, and no other placeholder feeds a full-rupiah value through it. No number was hand-typed, and the model, target and rating are unchanged.

challenges.section: fund record qc_justifications (drift.capex_pct) / 3. Financial analysis and forecasts
challenges.challenge: The answer recorded against the blocking drift.capex_pct gate still misstates its evidence (QC Q14, judge FIX 2). It calls the 29 October 2026 Rp149.2bn Bank Mega equipment credit "about 2% of 2025 capex" (it is 9.4% of FY2025 capex of Rp1,588.9bn [F11, S5] and 11.1% of 9M-2026 capex [F52]), says the flat 9M-2026 spend "includes the final batch payments" although S6 dates both fleet batches fully operational to end-September 2025, and calls the credit "replacement investment" although S10 describes it as a new heavy-equipment purchase ("untuk pembelian alat berat"). The 25% -> 16% fade itself survives on fleet completion [S6] and LT capex above D&A [F9], but an answer recorded against a BLOCK gate cannot overstate the evidence it rests on.
challenges.answer: Rewritten on its evidence. The Rp149.2bn Bank Mega credit is now stated as about 9.4% of FY2025 capex of Rp1,588.9bn [F11, S5] and 11.1% of 9M-2026 capex [F52], and as a new heavy-equipment purchase, not replacement [F105, S10]. The unsourced "final batch payments" claim is deleted; the fade to 16% LT rests on fleet completion (both batches fully operational by end-September 2025 [S6]) and on LT capex above D&A at 15% of revenue [F9]. The capex_pct basis is aligned to the same wording, the engine was re-run and fund record qc still shows drift.capex_pct justified with zero blocking flags.

challenges.challenge: The da_pct basis still says "fixed-asset depreciation of Rp861.96bn [F9, S5] plus right-of-use depreciation of Rp78.71bn [F10, S5]" (QC Q15, judge FIX 3). Since the Q10 fix F9 carries the combined FY2025 charge of Rp940.67bn (fund record: 861.96 + 78.71), so citing F9 for 861.96 and then adding F10 double-counts to Rp1,019.4bn and contradicts the fact registry. The model uses the combined Rp940.67bn (FY2025A EBITDA Rp1,667.1bn), so this is in the published assumption log only, but it is the line a reader would use to check the restatement.
challenges.answer: The basis now states the two printed components separately, fixed-asset depreciation of Rp861.96bn (S5 p.89) and right-of-use depreciation of Rp78.71bn (S5 p.92), and cites F9 only for their combined FY2025 total of Rp940.67bn, which is the figure the model uses. It says explicitly that adding F10 on top of F9 would double-count. Text only; no model change.

challenges.section: review record (C4, C5 and C13 responses) / published document
challenges.challenge: Several red-team response notes were written before the round-2 model changes and now contradict the final model, and cov_publish prints each challenge answer in the public document. C5 says "implied FY2027E growth of 0.36%"; the model's reverse DCF solves FY2027E growth at 2.9% (base 5.0% less 2.12pp [fund record reverse_dcf]) and §4 renders 2.9%. C13 says the current fundamental value is Rp286.9, the twelve-month value Rp331.4 and the price 0.77x; the final model has Rp269.8, Rp311.9 and 0.82x, which is what §4 and the summary render. C4 says terminal value is 68.6% of EV; the final model is 69.4%. The conclusions survive (2.9% is still below CPI 3.28%, and the price-cut framing holds), but the published record would carry numbers that exist nowhere in the package.
challenges.answer: The published review record is refreshed to the final model. C4 now reads 69.4% terminal value (was 68.6%); C5 reads implied FY2027E growth of 2.9% (was 0.36%) and states the 62.6% share against market capitalisation, with CPI at 3.28%; C13 reads Rp269.8 current value, Rp311.9 twelve-month value and 0.82x (was Rp286.9 / Rp331.4 / 0.77x). The C12 note was also stale against the same fact fix and now reads FY2025A D&A of Rp940.67bn and EBITDA of Rp1,667.1bn (was Rp1,588.4bn). No target, rating or model change.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull case shocks only revenue growth and gross margin and never re-rates GMR, although GMR is about 49% of DCF equity value; a resource statement validating the appraisal is worth up to ~Rp138/share before the lens. The market-implied ex-GMR operating value (~3.3x FY2026E EBITDA) and the Arutmin renewal option are also unpriced. C5, C7, C15.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear scenario (TP 324) still carries the full Rp5,380bn GMR bridge, so the single largest downside is never quantified. Also absent: the two-year volume decline (total overburden 193.85 to 138.63 Mbcm; KPC 122.09 to 102.16) against the 600 Mt RKAB and 1 Jan 2027 DSI transition; the Feb-2025 46.29% issuance at Rp75 and the Rp580 buyback as capital-allocation and ownership facts. C1, C6, C8, C9.

assumption_realism.note: Growth is never decomposed into volume and rate: the +10.5%/+8%/+6% path runs against the LK's project volumes and the 24% RKAB cut. FY2026E capex at 20% is below the 9M actual run (26.3% of revenue) and a subsidiary drew Rp149.2bn for heavy equipment on 30 Oct 2026. net_borrowing of Rp1,000bn contradicts the same paragraph's +Rp1,917bn. C1, C2, C3.

flags.justification: The fade rests on fleet completion and maintenance spending, not on a claim that capex has already fallen. Both fleet batches were fully operational by end-September 2025 [S6], so the peak build spend is behind the company; the 9M-2026 spend of Rp1,341.6bn was flat on 9M-2025 [F52, S4], and the Oct-2026 Rp149.2bn Bank Mega credit to a subsidiary is new heavy-equipment purchase, not replacement investment [F105, S10]. That credit is about 9.4% of FY2025 capex of Rp1,588.9bn [F11, S5] and 11.1% of 9M-2026 capex [F52], so it confirms continued fleet spend rather than a collapse in it. FY2026E is held at the 9M run-rate of 25% of revenue; the step to 16% LT is a gradual normalisation as the completed fleet is maintained, and LT 16% stays above D&A at 15% of revenue [F9], so the fleet is maintained rather than run down.
